title: Test doubles: stub, mock, spy and fake

videos.script: Most code talks to something a test should not touch. A carrier's API that charges per call. A mail server that sends real e-mail. A clock that will not stand still. {{collaborators}} A test double stands in for one of those during a test. This lesson names five kinds, and they differ in what the stand-in does. {{five}} A dummy fills a parameter and is never used. A stub answers with values you chose. A spy writes down how it was called. A mock checks the calls itself. A fake really works, with a shortcut, like a table kept in a list. {{kinds}} None of them fits unless the code leaves a seam, a place where the collaborator is handed in. You will see shipquote's seams, and what patching costs when there is none. {{seam}} Then the uncomfortable part. Every double is a claim about something real, and claims go stale. You will watch a mock pass while production breaks, and a stub stay green after the carrier changed its answer. {{drift}} And you will see the two habits that catch it: mocks built from the real class, and contract tests that ask the real service. {{contract}}
